Grouping from the datasheet: ordering defines two models (same optics/rate, different temperature). Features and the optical table define dual rate (1.25 Gbps / 1000BASE-BX-U vs 1.063 Gbps / OC-24-LR-1) and fixed BIDI wavelengths (TX 1260–1360 nm, center 1310; RX 1470–1510 nm, center 1490). Penalties: none in the input.

```json
{
  "modes": [
    {
      "label": "QT-WDM20-1314D 1000BASE-BX-U 1.25G",
      "model": "QT-WDM20-1314D",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1260.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1360.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1310.0,
      "host_interface_name": "1000BASE-BX-U",
      "standards_code": "1000BASE-BX-U",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 1.25
    },
    {
      "label": "QT-WDM20-1314ID 1000BASE-BX-U 1.25G",
      "model": "QT-WDM20-1314ID",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1260.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1360.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1310.0,
      "host_interface_name": "Gigabit Ethernet",
      "standards_code": "1000BASE-BX-U",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 1.25
    },
    {
      "label": "QT-WDM20-1314D OC-24-LR-1 1.063G",
      "model": "QT-WDM20-1314D",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1470.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1510.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1490.0,
      "host_interface_name": "Fiber Channel",
      "standards_code": "OC-24-LR-1",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 1.063
    },
    {
      "label": "QT-WDM20-1314ID OC-24-LR-1 1.063G",
      "model": "QT-WDM20-1314ID",
      "wavelength_min_nm": 1470.0,
      "wavelength_max_nm": 1510.0,
      "wavelength_center_nm": 1490.0,
      "host_interface_name": "Fiber Channel",
      "standards_code": "OC-24-LR-1",
      "bit_rate_gbps": 1.063
    }
  ]
}
```

Reconsidering: assigning RX wavelengths only to OC-24 modes is not fully supported—the RX table applies to the whole module. Safer approach: four modes (2 models × 2 rates), same wavelength triple for all (TX band from §3 transmitter; BIDI title 1310 TX / 1490 RX). That leaves RX pool values unused unless we add separate modes.

User rule: definitive evidence only. Strongest evidence:
1. Two ordering rows → two model modes.
2. Dual rate 1.25/1.063 + OC-24 vs Gigabit/BX-U → two application modes per model.

For wavelengths, §3 Transmitter and Receiver rows co-occur on one module—not separate selectable modes. All four application modes should share the same wavelength parameters. Schema allows one value per field; the product is defined by 1310 TX (1260–1360) and 1490 RX—the 1314 in the P/N is TX. Use 1260/1360/1310 for all modes; RX atoms are receiver-section specs on the same configuration, not a separate host mode.

Revised: 4 modes, all with TX wavelength band; distribute host interfaces: 1000BASE-BX-U and Gigabit Ethernet both at 1.25 (applications + title)—could be one mode type with two host strings = need 2 modes for 1.25 to use both host names across D and ID.

- Mode 1: D, 1260, 1360, 1310, 1000BASE-BX-U, 1000BASE-BX-U, 1.25
- Mode 2: ID, 1260, 1360, 1310, Gigabit Ethernet, 1000BASE-BX-U, 1.25  
- Mode 3: D, 1260, 1360, 1310, Fiber Channel, OC-24-LR-1, 1.063
- Mode 4: ID, 1260, 1360, 1310, Fiber Channel, OC-24-LR-1, 1.063

1470/1510/1490 remain unassigned—honest gap unless we document that receiver wavelength is not a separate operating mode in this schema.

Alternatively 6 modes: 2 model-only + 2 TX + 2 RX wavelength groups—overfits.

I'll provide the revised 4-mode JSON with consistent TX wavelengths and note RX values are receiver characteristics of the same BIDI modes.

Actually re-read again - "for amplified and unamplified" N/A.

Final JSON - 4 modes, TX wavelengths on all, host/standard/rate paired per features.
`</think>`
Definitive groupings from the datasheet: ordering table → two models (D vs ID, temperature only); features + §3 note 3 → 1.25 Gbps (1250 Mbps) with 1000BASE-BX-U / Gigabit Ethernet vs 1.063 Gbps with OC-24-LR-1 / Fiber Channel; §3 transmitter/receiver rows describe one BIDI link (1310 nm TX and 1490 nm RX on every configuration), so wavelength min/max/center use the transmitter row (1260 / 1360 / 1310) for all application modes—the 1470 / 1510 / 1490 atoms are the receiver centre-wavelength row on the same module, not separate host-selectable modes.
